title: Effectiveness of a Generate–Verify–Repair Pipeline with Batfish for LLM‑Generated Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We report a preregistered paired experiment (cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1) that evaluated whether a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline—shared initial LLM candidate (gpt-5-mini) + a deterministic Batfish‑style validator + at most one automated LLM repair—reduces deterministic‑verifier detected semantic/safety failures on intent→vendor‑CLI tasks. Planned N=300 pairs; 266 complete pairs were analysed after preregistered exclusions. Baseline pass-rate = 260/266 (97.744%); guarded (final GVR) pass-rate = 265/266 (99.624%). Paired difference = 0.018796992481203034; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625. Paired bootstrap (B=10,000, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601]. Repair was invoked for 6 tasks; median repair iterations per task = 0. Per‑episode latency was not recorded in per‑task artifacts and thus could not be evaluated. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the observed absolute improvement is small and did not meet the preregistered α=0.05 decision rule. We present preregistered design details, deterministic validator semantics, complete numeric outcomes, representative artifact‑grounded repair examples, contamination findings (no exact public duplicates flagged), and an evidence‑grounded discussion of limitations and implications.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are actively explored for network operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent→CLI translation, zero‑touch configuration synthesis, and automated maintenance workflows [1],[2]. Stochastic LLM generation can produce syntactic or semantic violations—missing commands, unsafe operation orderings, or constraint breaches—that create operational risk when executed on device CLIs. To reduce such risk, research and prototype pipelines propose interposing deterministic verifiers (e.g., Batfish or header‑space analysis) and bounded repair loops—generate–verify–repair (GVR)—so that only outputs passing a deterministic oracle are considered for application [3],[4].

Motivated by the limited preregistered, paired evaluations that instrument verifier‑triggered repair with archived deterministic traces, we preregistered and executed the following question: Does a GVR pipeline that uses a single sampled initial LLM candidate per task (shared_initial_candidate semantics), a deterministic Batfish‑style validator, and at most one automated LLM repair call reduce verifier‑detected semantic/safety failures relative to the same initial candidate without repair? Our principal contribution is a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired evaluation (study id cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1) that preserves the exact preregistered estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), reports exact paired contingency counts and tests, and provides representative before/after artifacts for auditability.
sections.related_work:
LLM applications in NetOps include intent→CLI translation and task‑oriented prototypes and benchmarks that study automated configuration generation and correctness [1]. Surveys and tutorials summarize opportunity spaces and failure modes for LLMs in network operations and AIOps and advocate grounding and verification components when moving toward automation [2]. Generate–verify–repair architectures have been proposed in code generation and regulated domains to produce deterministic validation guarantees via external oracles and bounded repair loops [3]. Network verification tools such as Batfish and header‑space analyses enable deterministic checks over network models and have been proposed or used as verifier components in LLM‑augmented NetOps prototypes [4]. Analyses of LLM requirements for synthesizing correct router configurations emphasize sequencing and vendor‑syntax difficulties and motivate verifier augmentation [5].

Our study differs by (a) using shared_initial_candidate semantics (the same initial sampled candidate is used for both baseline and guarded outcomes per preregistration), (b) archiving raw model traces and deterministic validator traces for each episode, and (c) reporting exact paired counts with preregistered inferential procedures.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The experiment was preregistered as cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1 (manifest SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under these semantics a single sampled initial model candidate is shared: baseline outcome = validator result on the initial candidate; guarded outcome = validator result after allowing at most one automated LLM repair for the same initial candidate if the validator initially fails. This design isolates the deterministic validator‑triggered repair effect for a fixed initial sample as preregistered.

Task bank and sampling: The preregistered task bank deterministically produced 300 intent→CLI pairs (150 Cisco‑like; 150 Juniper‑like) using a deterministic synthetic task generator combined with public NetConfEval‑style examples; per‑task manifest entries, generator ids, and generation seeds are archived. Inclusion/exclusion, retry, and missingness rules followed the preregistration. Deterministic exclusion logic removed 34 both‑arm provider/infrastructure failures (see analysis/missingness_summary.csv), leaving 266 complete paired units for the primary analysis.

Model and orchestration disclosure: Declared model version: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Archived model config fields include max_output_tokens=1024, maximum_attempts_per_call=1, provider=openai_responses, and temperature=null (unset). The orchestration adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Provider‑call accounting shows hosted_model_call_event_count=306 with 34 failed calls and stage counts: shared_initial_generation=300, repair=6 (six repair calls observed).

Deterministic validator semantics: The binary oracle used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. For each episode the validator performs CLI syntactic parsing/normalization, per‑task required‑sequence checks (expected_sequence vs parsed commands), constrained‑field touch checks (allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields), and reachability/constraint validation against the synthetic topology model. Validator traces archive parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation codes, and normalized_configuration. The validator’s binary pass/fail is the primary endpoint and is archived per episode in execution/scoring/*.json.

Repair loop mechanics and limits: Per preregistration the initial sampled candidate is shared across arms; if the validator fails that candidate, the guarded arm may invoke at most one automated LLM repair call. Repair prompts include the validator’s failure codes and task constraints; repair prompts and provider traces are archived when invoked. The one‑repair bound was preregistered to model a bounded automated corrective step analogous to a single automated attempt before escalation or human review.

Analysis plan and inferential methods: The primary confirmatory test is the exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes (α=0.05). Interval estimation uses a paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) as preregistered; the bootstrap CI was included to quantify paired‑difference magnitude and finite‑sample uncertainty beyond the discrete McNemar p‑value. Secondary estimands (preregistered) included median_repair_iterations_per_task and median end‑to‑end latency (latency could not be evaluated because per‑episode timing was not archived). Missingness handling followed the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule: pairs with both arms affected by provider/infrastructure failures were excluded from the primary analysis (34 such pairs). Sensitivity analyses treating excluded episodes as failures were executed as preregistered.
sections.results:
Execution accounting: Planned episodes = 600 (300 pairs × 2); completed episodes = 532; failed episodes = 68. Complete paired units analysed = 266; both_missing_pairs = 34 excluded per preregistration (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Provider/model call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation.json) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 306, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 272, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 34, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 272, and stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 6.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 266): baseline successes = 260; guarded final successes = 265. Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 260 (both pass), n10 = 5 (guarded pass only), n01 = 0 (baseline pass only), n00 = 1 (both fail). Observed proportions: baseline = 260/266 = 0.9774436090225563; guarded = 265/266 = 0.9962406015037594. Paired difference = 0.018796992481203034. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625 (preregistered α=0.05 decision → not significant). Paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) = [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601]; bootstrap parameters and seed are archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.

Repair activity and representative artifacts: Repair was invoked 6 times across the planned 300 tasks; median repair iterations per task = 0. Representative example: task‑000008 (execution/responses/task-000008-shared-initial.txt, sha256 = 89306095...) shows the shared initial candidate terminated with an incomplete final line "interface uplink2\n" and failed the validator; the guarded final artifact (execution/responses/task-000008-guarded.txt, sha256 = d52b7616f...) contains the corrected complete sequence and passed validation_after. All episode validator traces (execution/scoring/task-000008-*.json) archive concrete failure codes that triggered repair and the normalized_configuration accepted after repair. Repair prompts and repair provider traces for the six repairs are archived (refer to execution/provider_calls/ and execution/scoring/ entries).

Contamination and sensitivity: analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty—no exact public duplicates were flagged and none were excluded for contamination in the primary analysis. Sensitivity treating the 34 excluded both‑arm episodes as failures (conservative N=300 analysis) yields baseline = 260/300 = 0.866667 and guarded = 265/300 = 0.883333 with the same discordant counts (n10=5, n01=0) and exact McNemar p = 0.0625, confirming the primary inferential conclusion’s robustness to the preregistered conservative missingness handling.

Artifacts and hashes: Key archived artifacts and their SHA‑256 values are present in the evidence bundle (e.g., execution/raw_results.jsonl sha256 = 34fe154dde2a540f..., execution/model_configuration.json sha256 = 916b386bd80cbffb..., provenance/master_prompt.txt sha256 = 1872df1e1805d2d9...). The deterministic_reconciliation.json documents completed_episode_count, failed_episode_count, and provider call counts used above.
sections.discussion:
Statistical interpretation: The guarded GVR pipeline produced a small absolute increase in verifier pass‑rate (~1.88 percentage points). Under the preregistered exact McNemar test the improvement did not reach α=0.05 (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) narrowly excludes zero while McNemar does not reject; this divergence reflects finite‑sample discreteness of McNemar (it depends only on discordant counts n10 and n01) and the bootstrap’s empirical paired‑difference variability. We therefore report both inferential perspectives to enable balanced judgment on practical relevance vs formal hypothesis acceptance.

Operational implications and boundary conditions: Baseline single‑shot pass rate was high (~97.7%), leaving few failures for repair to correct; accordingly repair invocations were rare (6/300). For workloads with high first‑pass accuracy, the operational ROI of adding a bounded automated repair stage may be limited. Conversely, GVR may yield larger absolute gains when baseline first‑pass accuracy is lower or when verifier coverage is expanded to detect more failure types.

Threats to validity: Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics measure the effect of validator‑triggered repair on a fixed initial sample and do not evaluate independent multiple‑draw strategies or constrained first‑pass prompting (these were not executed under the preregistration and lie outside the estimand). Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite battery of syntactic/sequence/constraint checks; semantic violations outside that battery are undetected. External validity: tasks derive from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor dialect clusters (Cisco‑like, Juniper‑like); results may not generalize to other vendors, larger production topologies, or different difficulty distributions. Conclusion validity: small discordant counts (n10=5, n01=0) and exclusion of 34 pairs for infrastructure failures reduced precision and power; future studies should plan for greater discordance or larger N when baseline pass rates are expected to be high.

Design lessons and reproducibility recommendations: (1) When baseline pass rates are high, experimental designs should target lower‑baseline corpora or larger N to better quantify repair effectiveness. (2) Record per‑episode latency and pipeline timing to evaluate operational bounds (the preregistered latency endpoint could not be assessed because per‑task timing was not archived). (3) Expand and publish validator rule coverage to reduce construct‑validity uncertainty and enable measuring verifier false negatives. (4) Consider separate preregistered arms that contrast shared_initial_candidate semantics with independent multiple draws and constrained prompting to estimate alternative practical interventions; such arms must be explicitly preregistered because they change the estimand.

Concluding remark: The preregistered, artifact‑archived paired study shows a small guarded improvement that did not meet the preregistered exact‑McNemar decision rule (p=0.0625) while producing a narrow bootstrap CI excluding zero. All execution and analysis artifacts, validator traces, raw responses, and hash manifests are archived for reanalysis and follow‑on work.
sections.conclusion:
A preregistered paired experiment evaluated a GVR pipeline (gpt‑5‑mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + ≤1 automated repair) on intent→CLI tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Across 266 analysed pairs the guarded pipeline improved validator pass rate by 0.018796992481203034 but did not meet the preregistered exact‑McNemar α=0.05 decision rule (p=0.0625); a paired bootstrap CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) narrowly excludes zero. Repair calls were rare (6/300) and median repair iterations per task = 0. Per‑episode latency was not archived and therefore could not be assessed. All execution and analysis artifacts, including raw responses, validator traces, provider call accounting, and reconciliation manifests, are archived in the evidence bundle to support reanalysis.

References
[1] C. Wang, M. Scazzariello, A. Farshin, S. Ferlin, D. Kostić, and M. Chiesa, “NetConfEval: Can LLMs Facilitate Network Configuration?,” in Proceedings of ACM (NetConfEval), 2024, doi: 10.1145/3656296.
[2] S. Y. Long, J. Tan, B. Mao, F. Tang, Y. Li, M. Zhao, and N. Kato, “A Survey on Intelligent Network Operations and Performance Optimization Based on Large Language Models,” IEEE Commun. Surveys & Tutorials, 2025, doi: 10.1109/COMST.2025.3526606.
[3] R. Cadenas, “Convergent Correctness in Stochastic Code Generation: A Generate‑Verify‑Repair Architecture for Deterministic Validation of Autonomous AI Coding Agents in Regulated Environments,” SSRN, 2026, doi: 10.2139/ssrn.6754899.
[4] M. Brown, A. Fogel, D. Halperin, V. Heorhiadi, R. Mahajan, and T. Millstein, “Lessons from the evolution of the Batfish configuration analysis tool,” Proc. ACM (paper), 2023, doi: 10.1145/3603269.3604866.
[5] R. Mondal, A. Tang, R. Beckett, T. Millstein, and G. Varghese, “What do LLMs need to Synthesize Correct Router Configurations?,” Proc. ACM (paper), 2023, doi: 10.1145/3626111.3628194.

Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Preregistration: cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1 (manifest SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891). Nondeterminism disclosure: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset) and no deterministic sampling seed is archived; therefore nondeterministic sampling of model outputs cannot be excluded for the recorded provider calls. Execution and analysis artifacts, logs, and hash manifests are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the preregistration.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: both arms used the same single sampled initial candidate per preregistration; the estimand measures validator‑triggered repair benefit for that fixed initial sample and does not evaluate independent first‑pass generations or constrained first‑pass prompting strategies.

Missingness and sample reduction: planned N=300 pairs; after infrastructure/provider exclusions 266 pairs were complete and 34 both‑arm episodes were excluded per preregistered rules, reducing effective sample size and precision.
Small discordant counts: primary inference used exact McNemar with few discordants (n10=5, n01=0); conclusions are sensitive to inferential choice and limited power.
Validator coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite set of syntactic/semantic/reachability rules; semantic violations outside its coverage are possible and unmeasured.

Runtime nondeterminism and sampling: archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null and no deterministic seed; nondeterministic sampling cannot be excluded for recorded model calls.
H2 latency not evaluated: per‑episode end‑to‑end latency was not present in archived per‑task artifacts and therefore the preregistered latency bound (median ≤ 60 s) could not be assessed.

External validity: task corpus derives from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor‑dialect clusters; results do not imply universal benefit across other vendors, larger topologies, or production deployments.
